hero.lead: Africa’s most populous nation, 237.5 million strong, whose 2025 Eurobond drew more than $13 billion of orders for $2.35 billion of paper.

capital.heading: Nigeria borrows at scale and the world bids for it. Next, a full table in every home.

record.text: Total public debt at 31 March 2026, equal to $114.95 billion: external $51.90 billion, domestic $63.05 billion
Eurobonds: $1.25B due 2036 and $1.10B due 2046, priced 5 November 2025; peak order book over $13B
Reforms for Economic Stabilization to Enable Transformation (RESET): development policy financing, June 2024
Nigeria Actions for Investment and Jobs Acceleration (NAIJA): development policy financing for capital markets, the digital economy, power, trade, seed and revenue, June 2026
Indorama Eleme Fertilizer and Chemicals: a third urea line of 1.4 million tonnes a year and a shipping terminal, March 2024

register.name: Eurobonds, long 10-year and long 20-year
register.detail: Priced 5 November 2025 · $1.25 billion due 2036 · $1.10 billion due 2046 · Coupons/yields of 8.6308% and 9.1297%
register.note: Peak order book over $13 billion
register.text: Two dollar bonds sold on the international market to finance the 2025 fiscal deficit and other needs of the government. The peak order book of more than $13 billion was the largest Nigeria has achieved, more than five times the amount sold.

register.name: Sovereign Green Bond, third issuance
register.detail: Offer closed 18 June 2025 · ₦50 billion offered · ₦91.42 billion subscribed, 183% · Coupon 18.95%
register.note: Proceeds finance projects in the 2024 Appropriation Act
register.text: Nigeria’s third sovereign green bond, sold in naira and subscribed almost twice over; ₦47.355 billion was allotted. Its proceeds finance projects in the 2024 federal budget that support the nation’s climate commitments.

register.name: Agro-Climatic Resilience in Semi-Arid Landscapes (ACReSAL), additional financing
register.detail: Announced 6 November 2026 · Additional financing · 19 northern states and the Federal Capital Territory
register.note: 1.4 million hectares and 6.6 million people by 2031
register.text: Restores degraded landscapes, rehabilitates watersheds and improves erosion and flood management across northern Nigeria, reaching 1.4 million hectares and 6.6 million people by 2031. It protects the water, food and livelihoods of farming and herding families.

register.name: Nigeria Actions for Investment and Jobs Acceleration (NAIJA)
register.detail: Approved 29 June 2026 · Development policy financing · With the Country Partnership Framework 2026–2032
register.note: Capital markets, digital economy, power, trade, seed and revenue
register.text: Supports reforms that deepen capital markets, modernise the rules for the digital economy and e-governance, advance power sector reform, lower trade barriers, improve access to quality seed and raise domestic revenue. It was approved with a partnership framework that aims to expand energy access to 32 million Nigerians.

register.name: Sustainable Agricultural Value-Chains for Growth (AGROW)
register.detail: Approved 30 March 2026 · IDA credit
register.note: Up to one million farmers
register.text: Links smallholder farmers to agribusiness through matching grants, better seed and fertiliser systems and digital advice.

register.name: Fostering Inclusive Finance for MSMEs in Nigeria (FINCLUDE)
register.detail: Approved 19 December 2025 · IBRD loan $400 million · IDA credit $100 million · Up to $800 million in guarantees
register.note: Debt finance for 250,000 small firms, at least 150,000 led by women
register.text: Expands debt finance to 250,000 micro, small and medium enterprises, at least 150,000 of them led by women, and can issue up to $800 million in guarantees to draw in lending. Small firms employ most Nigerians, so it serves the livelihood standard.

register.name: Building Resilient Digital Infrastructure for Growth (BRIDGE)
register.detail: Approved 7 October 2025 · Concessional financing · Total project cost $1.6 billion
register.note: Fibre backbone from 35,000 to 125,000 km
register.text: Builds a nationwide fibre network through a company that is majority privately owned, to connect 38,800 public schools, 16,900 health facilities and 3,400 local government offices. It lays the links on which modern schooling, health care and work depend.

register.name: Hope for Quality Basic Education for All (HOPE-EDU)
register.detail: Approved 31 March 2025 · Global Partnership for Education co-financing $52.18 million
register.note: 29 million children in public primary schools
register.text: Supports basic education for 29 million children enrolled in public primary schools, 500,000 teachers and more than 65,000 schools. It serves the education standard where it begins.

register.name: Community Action for Resilience and Economic Stimulus (NG-CARES), additional financing
register.detail: Approved 31 March 2025 · Additional financing
register.note: More than 15 million direct beneficiaries so far
register.text: Extends a programme for poor and vulnerable households and communities that has reached more than 15 million direct beneficiaries. It serves the livelihood and food standards together.

register.name: Accelerating Nutrition Results in Nigeria (ANRIN 2.0)
register.detail: Approved 31 March 2025
register.note: Nutrition for mothers, adolescent girls and children under five
register.text: Increases the use of quality, low-cost nutrition services for pregnant women, nursing mothers, adolescent girls and children under five. The first phase reached more than 13 million children under five between 2018 and 2024; food sets Coverage in Nigeria.

register.name: Primary Healthcare Provision Strengthening Program (HOPE-PHC)
register.detail: Approved 26 September 2024 · IDA credit $500 million · Global Financing Facility grant $70 million
register.note: 40 million people
register.text: Strengthens primary health care for women, children and adolescents, benefiting 40 million people, especially the most vulnerable. It is the health standard at the front line of care.

register.name: Sustainable Power and Irrigation for Nigeria (SPIN)
register.detail: Approved 26 September 2024
register.note: Irrigation for 40,000 hectares; up to 950,000 people
register.text: Improves dam safety and brings new and better irrigation and drainage to 40,000 hectares, for up to 950,000 people in farming and herding households, and prepares a hydropower master plan. It serves the water, food and energy standards.

register.name: Reforms for Economic Stabilization to Enable Transformation (RESET)
register.detail: Approved 13 June 2024 · Development policy financing · Approved with the $750 million ARMOR revenue programme
register.note: Fiscal room and support for the poor
register.text: Supports reforms that strengthen economic policy, create fiscal room and protect the poor and the economically vulnerable. It was approved with a $750 million programme for revenue reform, in a $2.25 billion package.

register.name: Distributed Access through Renewable Energy Scale-up (DARES)
register.detail: Approved 14 December 2023 · IDA credit · Parallel financing: Global Energy Alliance for People and Planet $100 million, JICA $200 million
register.note: New or better electricity for more than 17.5 million Nigerians
register.text: Funds solar mini-grids and standalone solar to give more than 17.5 million Nigerians new or improved electricity and to replace more than 280,000 petrol and diesel generators. It is designed to draw in more than $1 billion of private capital for the energy standard.

register.name: Niger State Solar Energy Development Project
register.detail: Approved 16 June 2026 · 367th meeting of the Board of Executive Directors, Baku
register.note: Clean electricity and a more reliable supply
register.text: Expands clean electricity generation, makes power more reliable and diversifies the energy mix in Niger State. It serves the energy standard.

register.name: National Agricultural Growth Scheme – Agro-Pocket (NAGS-AP), phase II
register.detail: Announced 13 February 2026 · Loan · Four years from March 2026
register.note: Farm productivity, value chains and climate-smart farming
register.text: Scales up priority farm investments that raise productivity, strengthen value chains and spread climate-smart, data-driven farming. Food sets Coverage in Nigeria.

register.name: Special Agro-Industrial Processing Zones (SAPZ), phase II, first tranche
register.detail: Approved 1 December 2025 · Multi-tranche financing facility · First tranche covers 10 states
register.note: 1.1 million jobs expected across 10 states
register.text: Builds agro-industrial zones that process food close to the farm. Phase II is planned in three tranches to reach an additional 27 states, and the first tranche is expected to create 1.1 million jobs, 200,000 of them direct.

register.name: Economic Governance and Energy Transition Support Programme, phase II
register.detail: Approval announced 26 November 2025 · Policy-based loan for fiscal years 2024 and 2025
register.note: Public finance, power sector reform and the energy transition
register.text: Supports reforms in public financial management, the power sector and the energy transition plan, with steps to widen energy access. It serves the energy standard through reform.

register.name: Solar hybrid mini-grids, five renewable energy service companies
register.detail: Announced 29 April 2026 · IFC and Norfund loans · Concessional loans from the IDA Private Sector Window · 315 sites
register.note: Electricity for 2.9 million people
register.text: Loans of up to $83.2 million to Darway Coast, GVE Projects, Prado Power, PriVida Power and StarTimes Energy for 315 solar hybrid mini-grids, with estimated capital spending of $271 million. They bring electricity to homes and businesses in underserved communities.

register.name: Indorama Eleme Fertilizer and Chemicals, third urea line
register.detail: Announced 22 March 2024 · IFC loan $215.5 million · $940 million mobilised from development finance institutions and commercial banks
register.note: 1.4 million tonnes of urea a year
register.text: Finances a third urea fertiliser line and a new shipping terminal in Port Harcourt. More fertiliser made in Nigeria supports farm yields and the food standard.

assets.heading: Five assets no balance sheet counts.

items.name: The People
items.label: Citizens, 2025
items.text: 64 in every hundred live in towns and cities; the rest live on the land they farm and fish.
items.alt: A busy open-air market street in Lagos, traders and shoppers seen at a distance

items.name: The Land
items.label: Of land in farms and pasture
items.text: The land that feeds the nation, and the first place a citizen dividend can be earned.
items.alt: Smallholder farms of cassava and maize in the green Middle Belt of Nigeria

items.name: The Forest
items.label: Of land under forest
items.text: Standing forest holds the water, soil and carbon that the world will pay to keep.
items.alt: Dense tropical rainforest in Cross River State, Nigeria, morning mist in the canopy

items.name: The Water
items.label: Renewable fresh water per person
items.text: Below the scarcity line of 1,000 cubic metres: every drop must be stored, treated and reused.
items.alt: The wide brown Niger River at its confluence with the Benue near Lokoja, Nigeria

items.name: The Power
items.label: Of energy from renewables, 2021
items.text: Sun, wind, water and biomass already carry part of the load; the rest is the opportunity.
items.alt: Rows of solar panels of a village mini-grid in northern Nigeria under a bright sky

items.name: Babban Gona
items.text: An agri-tech company whose franchise model lets leading smallholder farmers in northern Nigeria run micro-enterprises that supply their peers with inputs and working capital, with credit, training, harvest, storage and market support. British International Investment committed $7.5 million of debt to it in 2025.

items.name: Darway Coast Nigeria
items.text: A renewable energy service company building solar hybrid mini-grids for homes and businesses in underserved communities. In April 2026 it was one of five developers in an $83.2 million IFC and Norfund financing, with $25 million of loans for its own sites.

items.name: NSIA Advanced Medical Services (MedServe)
items.text: A wholly owned health company of the Nigeria Sovereign Investment Authority that runs diagnostic and cancer care services. In February 2026 IFC committed about ₦14.2 billion ($24.5 million) towards a $154.1 million expansion into more than a dozen new diagnostic and treatment centres.

items.name: LAPO Microfinance Bank
items.text: One of Nigeria’s largest microfinance institutions, serving more than one million clients through more than 500 branches in all 36 states, with lending focused on women entrepreneurs, nano businesses and smallholder farmers. In April 2026 IFC disclosed a proposed senior loan of up to $10 million in naira.
